title: 4 Planets You Could Never Visit
next: Tomorrow: What if the Moon disappeared?

lines.say: Hey, space cadets! Captain Cosmo here, with the whole Cosmozibs crew!
Bolt here! I bring the numbers!
And I'm Tik! Stay until the end, because every planet has a quiz!
Today we visit four planets you could never, ever visit!
One is hotter than an oven. One has no ground at all. One has the wildest winds. And one... might rain glass!
Here's our map! Venus is the second planet from the Sun.
Jupiter is number five. And Neptune is all the way out at number eight!
And our last planet is so far away, it's not even on this map!
Hmph. Sounds like a terrible holiday.
Tick tock, let's go!

short.title: This Planet Is Hotter Than an Oven!

lines.say: This planet is hotter than an oven... and it's not even the closest to the Sun!
Wait... WHAT? How could this happen?!
Meet Venus! It's almost the same size as Earth. It's our next-door neighbor!
But Venus is wrapped in a super thick blanket of clouds. And that blanket traps the heat, like a car parked in the sun!
I did the math! The ground on Venus is about four hundred and sixty seven degrees Celsius!
That's way hotter than the oven in my kitchen!
It's even hotter than Mercury, the planet closest to the Sun!
Hmph. Still not as hot as me after a crash.
Bonus fact! The air on Venus pushes down really, really hard.
Standing there would feel like being more than nine hundred meters deep in the ocean!
My ears hurt just thinking about it!
Want more? Venus has no moon at all!
No moon? Who does it play with at night?
And its clouds are not made of water. They are made of sulfuric acid!
Acid clouds? Nope, nope, nope!
But here's the cool part. You can see Venus from your own window! After the Sun and the Moon, it's the brightest thing in our sky.
And here's the weirdest part. One day on Venus is longer than one whole year on Venus!
One spin takes two hundred and forty three Earth days. One trip around the Sun takes two hundred and twenty five.
Quiz time! On Venus, where does the Sun rise? In the east... in the west... or never?

show.q: Where does the Sun rise on Venus?

lines.say: In the west! Venus spins backwards, so the Sun rises in the west.
Next stop: a planet where you can't even stand up!

short.title: You Can't Land on This Planet!

lines.say: If you tried to land on this planet... there would be nowhere to land!
No ground? How could this happen?!
This is Jupiter, the biggest planet in our solar system.
Jupiter is a gas giant. It has no real surface. Just swirling gases and liquids!
A spaceship that dived in would get crushed and melted long before it reached the middle.
And it's HUGE! About one thousand Earths could fit inside Jupiter!
One thousand?! That's crazy!
Finally, a planet big enough for my ego.
Bonus fact! See that red spot? It's a giant storm!
The Great Red Spot is about twice as wide as Earth. And people have watched it for more than three hundred years!
A storm older than my grandma's grandma!
Jupiter also has a LOT of moons. One hundred and fifteen of them!
Its biggest moon, Ganymede, is the biggest moon in the whole solar system. It's even bigger than the planet Mercury!
A moon bigger than a planet? That's crazy!
Hmph. Show-off.
Quiz time! How long is one day on Jupiter? Ten hours, twenty four hours, or one hundred hours?

show.q: How long is a day on Jupiter?

lines.say: About ten hours! Jupiter has the shortest day of any planet.
Hold on to your helmets. Next up: the windiest world!

short.title: The Windiest Planet in the Solar System!

lines.say: This planet has the wildest winds in the whole solar system!
Windier than my hair dryer?
Way windier! This is Neptune, the farthest planet from the Sun.
Its winds blow at more than two thousand kilometers per hour!
That's about three times stronger than the winds on Jupiter.
That's crazy! You'd fly away like a kite!
Finally, something faster than me.
Bonus fact! Neptune is so far away, sunlight needs about four hours to get there.
To reach Earth, sunlight only needs about eight minutes!
Here's a cool story. Neptune was found with math!
Scientists calculated where a hidden planet should be. In eighteen forty six, Johann Galle looked there... and found Neptune on his very first night!
Math found a planet? I'm doing my homework right now!
And Neptune looks blue because a gas called methane soaks up the other colors and bounces back blue.
Only one spacecraft has ever flown past Neptune. Voyager Two, in nineteen eighty nine!
Quiz time! How long is one year on Neptune? One year, sixty five years, or one hundred and sixty five years?

show.q: How long is a year on Neptune?

lines.say: One hundred and sixty five Earth years! Nobody alive today is even one Neptune year old!
And now... the strangest planet of them all.

short.title: On This Planet It Rains Glass Sideways!

lines.say: On this planet, it might rain glass... sideways!
Glass?! SIDEWAYS?! How could this happen?!
This planet is not in our solar system. It's an alien world going around another star!
Scientists think its high clouds are full of tiny bits of glassy stuff called silicates.
And the winds blow up to eight thousand seven hundred kilometers per hour!
So the glass rain flies sideways! Ouch!
Note to self. Never go on holiday there.
Bonus fact! From far away, this planet looks deep blue, a bit like Earth.
But that blue comes from a hazy, burning hot sky. Not from an ocean!
This planet is about sixty three light years away from us.
And it's super hot. In the daytime it's more than a thousand degrees Celsius!
It's so close to its star that one side always faces the star, and the other side is always dark!
Always daytime on one side? I'd never have to go to bed!
You'd melt first, buddy.
Quiz time! Which is the hottest planet in our solar system? Mercury, Venus, or Jupiter?
Venus! Did you remember it from the start?
Speed round! Five quick facts. Ready? Go!
One! Venus is named after the Roman goddess of love and beauty.
Two! Jupiter is named after the king of the gods.
Three! Neptune is named after the Roman god of the sea.
Four! One year on Jupiter takes about twelve Earth years.
Five! Jupiter has rings too! Voyager One discovered them in nineteen seventy nine.
Whoa. My brain is full of space now!
That's four planets you could never visit! Which one was your favorite?
Now it's your turn! If you HAD to visit one of these planets, which one would you pick? Think about it!
I'd pick the one with the biggest crater. Obviously.
Tomorrow: what if the Moon disappeared?!

show.text: TOMORROW: WHAT IF THE MOON DISAPPEARED?

lines.say: Subscribe and join the crew. See you tomorrow, space cadets!
